packs.title: Historic rooms, source records and park paths
packs.promise: Read a historic house, collect city evidence and make from actual public paths.

q.s: Give a short park view four lines of your own.
st: Choose a safe opened path position near the recorded City-Brooks greenway area. Keep bicycle and walking circulation clear.
Notice one path edge, one visible texture and one sound that is actually present. No flower, bird, lake reflection or season-specific color is necessary.
Write four original postcard lines: begin with the broad path view, move to your texture and sound, and finish with a small detail you would want to remember.
Revise one line so it reflects today’s observation more precisely. Add a brief note showing which detail supplied each line; leave the park as you found it.

q.s: Collect the identities of three sources that describe this city.
st: Find the opened Baton Rouge Room and choose three currently readable records about Baton Rouge or its history. Use public reading materials, a displayed item or public Digital Archive records belonging to this collection; do not request private personal documents.
For each, note the title or item name, responsible creator or collection, date if stated and source form. Record an absent date as not stated rather than supplying one.
Write one city-specific subject each record helps investigate. Keep notes brief and paraphrased; different available items can replace a fixed title or inaccessible stored document.
Arrange your records into a small reading path and explain what different evidence the second and third add. Leave physical materials according to collection directions.

q.s: Put a material named by a label beside what you can see.
st: Choose three different currently readable artwork-and-label records in the admitted galleries, staying outside barriers.
For each, remember the title and artist as stated, one named material or process, and one detail you can actually observe. Do not infer a hidden material by touching it.
Compare two works: describe one visible difference beside their documented materials. Keep your interpretation distinct from an artist’s stated intention.
After leaving, write your three brief records and one comparison from memory, or use visitor-permitted notes. Paraphrase rather than reproducing long label text or collection images.

packs.title: Downtown riverfront and Capitol afternoons
packs.promise: Follow architecture, hands-on exhibits and public grounds across two downtown afternoons.

q.s: Collect what changes when you use a real exhibit control.
st: In the opened STEAM Station, choose three available visitor-operated exhibit controls from the current Rube Goldberg Ball Wall, Video Microscopes, Interactive Periodic Table or Everbright, following each station’s directions.
At each, make one permitted change and observe what actually happens. Record the input, the visible response and one limit in what your short observation can explain.
At one available station, make a second permitted change and compare the response. Do not take apart equipment, add a personal sample or claim an experiment proves more than you observed.

Write your three input-and-response records and one comparison after the visit, or use notes where current gallery directions permit. Keep the task your own rather than copying the operator’s question sheet.

q.s: Let a dry river path become an outward view and a return.
st: Begin at a permitted position on the opened upper paved promenade. Choose a comfortable short outward-and-return route, using actual signs and barriers rather than following a map line into a restricted area.
Walk north at your own pace toward the recorded short-turn area, noticing a change between the path, river view and downtown edge without needing a particular vessel or water level.
Turn at that area or earlier if current conditions require it, then return along the same opened dry path. Keep shared circulation and bridge approaches clear.
Write two actual observations, your real turnaround and one feature you noticed differently on the return. The route estimate is not a requirement to match an elapsed time.

q.s: Make a new pattern from a small historic building’s exterior.
st: Find the powder magazine from the linked grounds and historic-building information, staying on opened public exterior paths.
Notice two actual exterior shapes or material relationships, such as a roof edge meeting a wall or a repeated opening. Keep architectural description separate from a guess about stored contents.
Reduce those details to two original simple marks. Arrange them into a four-square pattern on your own page, or write a precise sequence if drawing is uncomfortable.
Revise one square so the pattern still connects to an observed detail. Add the DDD’s 1838 date as a separate source note and label your invented pattern as your own.
